lines.text: A circle of radius four sits snugly inside a triangle. How big can that triangle be?
lines.caption: A circle of radius four sits snugly inside a triangle. How big can that triangle be?

lines.text: One tiny slip here gives you exactly half the right answer.
lines.caption: One tiny slip here gives you exactly half the right answer.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee. Let's go triangle hunting!
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee. Let's go triangle hunting!

lines.text: A triangle has whole-number sides. Its inscribed circle has radius four.
lines.caption: A triangle has whole-number sides. Its inscribed circle has radius four.

lines.text: The circle touches A B and A C at the points six from A.
lines.caption: The circle touches A B and A C at the points six from A.

lines.text: What's the largest possible perimeter?
lines.caption: What's the largest possible perimeter?

lines.text: Your choices: forty-two, sixty, eighty-one, one hundred fifty, and one hundred sixty-two.
lines.caption: Your choices: forty-two, sixty, eighty-one, one hundred fifty, and one hundred sixty-two.

lines.text: So: radius four, six from A to each touch point, and we want the BIGGEST perimeter.
lines.caption: So: radius four, six from A to each touch point, and we want the BIGGEST perimeter.

lines.text: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Circle fact: two tangent pieces from one point are always equal.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Circle fact: two tangent pieces from one point are always equal.

lines.text: So both pieces at A are six. At corner B, call the two equal pieces y. At C, call them z.
lines.caption: So both pieces at A are six. At corner B, call the two equal pieces y. At C, call them z.

lines.text: Each side is two pieces: A B is six plus y, A C is six plus z, and B C is y plus z.
lines.caption: Each side is two pieces: A B is six plus y, A C is six plus z, and B C is y plus z.

lines.text: A B is whole, so y is whole. A C is whole, so z is whole.
lines.caption: A B is whole, so y is whole. A C is whole, so z is whole.

lines.text: Half the perimeter is one piece from each corner: six plus y plus z. Call it s.
lines.caption: Half the perimeter is one piece from each corner: six plus y plus z. Call it s.

lines.text: Now find the area two ways. Way one: join the center to each corner.
lines.caption: Now find the area two ways. Way one: join the center to each corner.

lines.text: Three small triangles! Each has a side as its base, and the radius, four, as its height.
lines.caption: Three small triangles! Each has a side as its base, and the radius, four, as its height.

lines.text: Adding them gives one over two times four times the perimeter. That's four times s.
lines.caption: Adding them gives one over two times four times the perimeter. That's four times s.

lines.text: Way two: Heron's formula. The area is the square root of s times s minus each side.
lines.caption: Way two: Heron's formula. The area is the square root of s times s minus each side.

lines.text: The magic: s minus a side leaves one tangent piece. That's six, y and z!
lines.caption: The magic: s minus a side leaves one tangent piece. That's six, y and z!

lines.text: So Heron gives the square root of six times s times y times z.
lines.caption: So Heron gives the square root of six times s times y times z.

lines.text: Set the two areas equal, square, and divide by s.
lines.caption: Set the two areas equal, square, and divide by s.

lines.text: Sixteen times s equals six y z. Halve it: eight times s equals three y z.
lines.caption: Sixteen times s equals six y z. Halve it: eight times s equals three y z.

lines.text: Put in six plus y plus z for s: forty-eight plus eight y plus eight z equals three y z.
lines.caption: Put in six plus y plus z for s: forty-eight plus eight y plus eight z equals three y z.

lines.text: Let's get z alone. Move eight z to the left, then pull out the z.
lines.caption: Let's get z alone. Move eight z to the left, then pull out the z.

lines.text: So z equals eight y plus forty-eight, over three y minus eight.
lines.caption: So z equals eight y plus forty-eight, over three y minus eight.

lines.text: The top is positive, so the bottom must be too: y is at least three.
lines.caption: The top is positive, so the bottom must be too: y is at least three.

lines.text: Make a table! At y equals three, z is seventy-two over one, so seventy-two.
lines.caption: Make a table! At y equals three, z is seventy-two over one, so seventy-two.

lines.text: At four, z is eighty over four, which is twenty.
lines.caption: At four, z is eighty over four, which is twenty.

lines.text: Five and six give eighty-eight over seven and ninety-six over ten. Not whole!
lines.caption: Five and six give eighty-eight over seven and ninety-six over ten. Not whole!

lines.text: At seven, z is one hundred four over thirteen, which is eight.
lines.caption: At seven, z is one hundred four over thirteen, which is eight.

lines.text: At eight, z is seven: a flip. Now z is below y, so only flips are left.
lines.caption: At eight, z is seven: a flip. Now z is below y, so only flips are left.

lines.text: So s equals eighty-one, thirty and twenty-one. Doubled: one hundred sixty-two, sixty and forty-two.
lines.caption: So s equals eighty-one, thirty and twenty-one. Doubled: one hundred sixty-two, sixty and forty-two.

lines.text: The biggest perimeter is one hundred sixty-two. That's choice E!
lines.caption: The biggest perimeter is one hundred sixty-two. That's choice E!

lines.text: Here's a slicker way: make a product. Multiply both sides by three.
lines.caption: Here's a slicker way: make a product. Multiply both sides by three.

lines.text: The right side becomes one hundred forty-four. Now add sixty-four to both sides.
lines.caption: The right side becomes one hundred forty-four. Now add sixty-four to both sides.

lines.text: The left side factors! Three y minus eight, times three z minus eight, equals two hundred eight.
lines.caption: The left side factors! Three y minus eight, times three z minus eight, equals two hundred eight.

lines.text: Each factor plus eight must divide by three. Let's test the factor pairs of two hundred eight.
lines.caption: Each factor plus eight must divide by three. Let's test the factor pairs of two hundred eight.

lines.text: Two and eight fail. One, four and thirteen pass, and so do their partners.
lines.caption: Two and eight fail. One, four and thirteen pass, and so do their partners.

lines.text: Same three triangles! One times two hundred eight gives y equals three, z equals seventy-two.
lines.caption: Same three triangles! One times two hundred eight gives y equals three, z equals seventy-two.

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you want every answer without wondering where to stop.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When you want every answer without wondering where to stop.

lines.text: Now the traps. Forty-two and sixty are real triangles with radius four, just not the biggest.
lines.caption: Now the traps. Forty-two and sixty are real triangles with radius four, just not the biggest.

lines.text: Eighty-one equals s, only HALF the perimeter. That's the tiny slip!
lines.caption: Eighty-one equals s, only HALF the perimeter. That's the tiny slip!

lines.text: One hundred fifty is what you'd get if you left out the two sixes at corner A.
lines.caption: One hundred fifty is what you'd get if you left out the two sixes at corner A.

lines.text: Now the circle has radius three, and the touch points are four from A.
lines.caption: Now the circle has radius three, and the touch points are four from A.

lines.text: Whole-number sides again. What's the largest perimeter?
lines.caption: Whole-number sides again. What's the largest perimeter?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The area is three times s, and also the square root of s times four y z.
lines.caption: Let's check. The area is three times s, and also the square root of s times four y z.

lines.text: Square, divide by s: nine times s equals four y z. Put in four plus y plus z for s.
lines.caption: Square, divide by s: nine times s equals four y z. Put in four plus y plus z for s.

lines.text: Get z alone: z equals nine y plus thirty-six, over four y minus nine.
lines.caption: Get z alone: z equals nine y plus thirty-six, over four y minus nine.

lines.text: Again y is at least three. Three gives sixty-three over three, so z is twenty-one!
lines.caption: Again y is at least three. Three gives sixty-three over three, so z is twenty-one!

lines.text: Four and five don't work. Six gives ninety over fifteen, which is six. Then z drops below y.
lines.caption: Four and five don't work. Six gives ninety over fifteen, which is six. Then z drops below y.

lines.text: So s is twenty-eight or sixteen, perimeter fifty-six or thirty-two. The largest is fifty-six!
lines.caption: So s is twenty-eight or sixteen, perimeter fifty-six or thirty-two. The largest is fifty-six!

lines.text: It's the seven, twenty-four, twenty-five right triangle. Fantastic work!
lines.caption: It's the seven, twenty-four, twenty-five right triangle. Fantastic work!

lines.text: The big idea: tangent pieces from one corner are equal, so a few letters name every side.
lines.caption: The big idea: tangent pieces from one corner are equal, so a few letters name every side.

lines.text: Then find the area two ways: radius times half the perimeter, and Heron's formula.
lines.caption: Then find the area two ways: radius times half the perimeter, and Heron's formula.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
